build_spec:
# Documents — Build Specification

## Overview

Documents is the **artifact-by-reference** pattern packaged as an app. Every document-shaped output (itinerary, letter, report, plan, proposal) lives as a markdown SOURCE FILE at `docs/<slug>.md`; the bot replies with a short summary and the path; revisions are targeted edits applied by the app's script (one section, or one phrase); the deliverable (PDF / HTML) is rendered by code from the source; attachments go by path. History carries the path and a content hash per revision, never the text twice.

Why: re-emitting a whole document through the model on every revision was the single most expensive habit in a measured week of personal-assistant use. This app removes the habit by giving the bot a cheaper move for every step of document work.

## Files (shipped as a files-pack — do NOT rewrite them)

This package ships its files in `gallery/documents/files/`; the install copies them verbatim (no placeholders). Nothing here needs an LLM to build.

```
scripts/documents.py     ← the one CLI (stdlib only)
docs/README.md           ← the docs/ convention
```

**Phase 4.5 owns materialization.** The `## Documents — write by reference` section of AGENTS.md is installed by the `documents-write-by-reference` session instruction (mechanism `oc_session_instruction`) with the evolve-managed marker. Do NOT write AGENTS.md sections during the Build phase — pre-writing without markers breaks clobber protection and uninstall.

## The CLI

```
python3 scripts/documents.py new <slug> [--title T] [--from FILE|-] [--force]
python3 scripts/documents.py show <slug> [--section "Heading"]
python3 scripts/documents.py outline <slug>
python3 scripts/documents.py edit <slug> --section "Heading" (--body-file F|- | --append-file F|- | --delete) [--create [--level N]]
python3 scripts/documents.py edit <slug> --find TEXT --replace TEXT [--all]
python3 scripts/documents.py render <slug> [--format both|pdf|html]
python3 scripts/documents.py summary <slug>
python3 scripts/documents.py log <slug>
python3 scripts/documents.py list
python3 scripts/documents.py status
```

All paths are relative to the bot's workspace root; the script resolves the workspace as the parent of its own `scripts/` directory, so it runs correctly from any cwd.

### Contract

- `new` refuses to overwrite an existing document without `--force`. It records revision 1.
- `edit --section` matches a heading by text (case-insensitive); the section spans to the next heading of the same or higher level, so sub-headings belong to their parent. A missing section lists the headings that exist; `--create` appends a new one.
- `edit --find/--replace` requires exactly one match unless `--all`, and says how many it found otherwise.
- Every `edit` prints a bounded unified diff (40 lines) and the summary block, then records a revision with `+added -removed` line counts.
- `render` writes `docs/<slug>.pdf` and `docs/<slug>.html` atomically (same content for the same source; only the footer's render stamp moves) and records the render on the latest revision. The PDF is PDF 1.4 with the base-14 Helvetica/Courier fonts and WinAnsi text — no dependencies.
- `status` is read-only and exits 0 even on a workspace with no docs/ yet (this is the verification-harness probe).

### The summary block

Every writing command ends by printing:

```
<Title> (docs/<slug>.md) — rev N, W words, S sections: A, B, C
Changed: +a -r lines (<what>)        ← edits only
Rendered: HTML docs/<slug>.html, PDF docs/<slug>.pdf
```

That block is what the bot relays to the user. It is the whole point: the reply is a few lines, not the document.

## Markdown subset

Headings (`#`…`######`), paragraphs, bullet and numbered lists (with continuation lines), fenced code, `>` quotes, horizontal rules, pipe tables, and inline **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](url). Anything else renders as a paragraph.

## Revision log

`docs/.revisions/<slug>.json`: `{slug, revisions: [{n, ts, op, detail, sha256, bytes, words, added_lines, removed_lines, renders{}, rendered_at?}]}`. Hashes and sizes only — never document text.

## Test sequence

```bash
python3 -m py_compile scripts/documents.py
python3 scripts/documents.py status
printf '# Test\n\n## A\n\nhello\n' | python3 scripts/documents.py new smoke --from -
printf 'goodbye\n' | python3 scripts/documents.py edit smoke --section A --body-file -
python3 scripts/documents.py render smoke
test -s docs/smoke.pdf && test -s docs/smoke.html && echo OK
```

All steps must exit 0.

install.body:
For any document-shaped output (itinerary, letter, report, plan, proposal): the document is a FILE, never a block of text in your reply.

- New: write the markdown to `docs/<slug>.md` with `python3 scripts/documents.py new <slug> --title "..." --from -` (content on stdin).
- Reply with the summary block the script prints (title, sections, word count, path) — a few lines, not the document.
- Revise: change only the part asked for — `python3 scripts/documents.py edit <slug> --section "Heading" --body-file -` (or `--find "old" --replace "new"`). Never rewrite or re-paste the whole document.
- Render: `python3 scripts/documents.py render <slug>` writes `docs/<slug>.pdf` and `.html`; attach by path (e.g. gmail_send attachments).
- Show or read: `outline <slug>`, `show <slug> --section "Heading"`, or send the rendered file — do not print or paste the whole document. `list` finds existing documents.

scheduled_actions.summary: One evolve-managed AGENTS.md section (under 1 KB) that tells the bot to keep documents in files, reply with summary + path, revise by targeted edit, render by script and attach by path. Zero heartbeat cost; no cron.

trigger_recognition.pattern: When the user asks for anything document-shaped — an itinerary, a letter, a report, a plan, a proposal, a memo — or asks to change, revise, render, or send one that already exists.

usage.how_to_use: Create with `new` (markdown on stdin), then relay the summary block. For any change, use `edit` on the one section or phrase that changes and relay the diff stats — never rewrite the document. Use `render` for a PDF/HTML and attach by path. Use `outline`/`show --section` to look at part of a document instead of reading the whole file.
